answer_1.quote: We systematically investigate how existing MT metrics assess high-quality (HQ) correct translations ... We find that automatic metrics struggle to distinguish between translations for a given source, especially when comparing HQ translations...

answer_2.quote: We first note that the correlation observed on the entire (NO-GROUPING ALL) and the subsampled datasets ... Metrics exhibit only a low-to-fair correlation with human judgments when evaluating translations for the same source.

answer_3.quote: GEMBA-MQM, a GPT-based QE metric, achieves the highest F1 score in detecting the HQ translations with no errors (HQ-ZERO).
methods: quality estimation using GPT‑4 as post‑hoc evaluator

answer_4.quote: Human evaluation study by the Conference on Machine Translation (WMT) ... the Multidimensional Quality Metrics framework relies on explicit error judgments (error types and severities) ... We rely on human MQM annotations as the gold standard for identifying high-quality translations.
answer_4.guideline: MQM guidelines that require annotators to label error types and severities (major vs. minor) within source‑translation spans.
